title: Risotto ai Funghi Porcini
subtitle: Dried porcini and parmesan risotto
excerpt: Arborio rice cooked slowly in porcini-infused stock until creamy. The dried porcini provide a depth of flavour that fresh mushrooms cannot match, the soaking liquid is as important as the mushrooms themselves.

recipe.sourceNotes: Risotto ai funghi porcini is one of the great autumn dishes of northern Italy, particularly Lombardy, Piedmont, and Emilia-Romagna. Dried porcini are used in preference to fresh because the drying concentrates their flavour, and the soaking liquid, dark and intensely earthy, becomes part of the cooking stock.

recipeTools.notes: Wide and heavy for even heat distribution.

content.text: Risotto ai funghi porcini is one of the few dishes where dried is really better than fresh. The dried porcini, soaked in hot water for 20 minutes, give up an intensely earthy, savoury liquid that becomes the base of your stock. Add that liquid to your vegetable stock, strain out any grit, and cook the risotto in it. The rice absorbs the porcini flavour from the first ladle.

Soak the dried porcini in 300 ml of hot water for 20 minutes. Lift them out, squeeze out the liquid, and chop roughly. Strain the soaking liquid through a fine sieve lined with kitchen paper and add to the hot stock.

Heat 1 tablespoon of the butter and the olive oil in a wide, heavy saucepan over medium heat. Cook the onion for 8 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and thyme and cook for 1 minute. Add the chestnut mushrooms and cook for 5 minutes until softened. Add the rehydrated porcini and cook for 2 more minutes.
Add the rice and stir for 2 minutes until the grains are coated in the butter and look slightly translucent at the edges. Pour in the wine and stir until it has absorbed completely.

Begin adding the hot stock a ladleful at a time, stirring after each addition and waiting until it has almost absorbed before adding the next. This process takes 18 to 20 minutes. The finished risotto should be creamy and flow like thick porridge; the rice should have a very slight bite at the centre.
Remove from the heat. Add the remaining butter and the grated parmesan. Stir vigorously for 1 minute. Cover and rest for 2 minutes. Taste for salt and pepper. Serve in warm bowls with extra parmesan.
